page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes and no headings. The running head sits at the top, with the page number at the top right. Nothing below the text except a stray mark.

main_text.p: gloriam, dolentque quòd plebs defertis sa-cerdotibus & scribis Domino adhæreret. Adiunt ergo confertim Pharisæi. Et quamquam insidias Christo tendunt, & dolosè eum adoriuntur ut circumueniant. utiliter tamen nobis cessit eorum malitia[?]: ficuti Dominus mirificè in tuorum utilitatem convertere novit, quæcunque ad veræ doctrinæ subversionem machinantur impii. Nam hac occasione soluta fuit quæstio, quam pariebat repudii libertas, & de sacro ac infolu-bili[?] coniugii nexu certa lex tradita. Inde autem arrepta est captionis ansa, quia in utranque partem secundum ipsos non nisi o-diosa esse poterat responsio. Nam quæstio admodum insidiosa est, ut si neget Christus atque damnet divortium, objiciant ei Mo-sem, clamentque, impiè ab ipso legem abrogari, Deut.24. quæ permittit quavis de cau-sa dare repudii libellū, ac dimittere: sin per-mittat simpliciter, dicant esse magistrum li-centiæ & corruptelæ morum, imo lenonem potius quàm Dei prophetam, qui sic viro-rum libidini indulgeat: aut secum pugnare, quum prius docuerit, non licere repudium,{*} Matth.5. Hoc quidem animis conceperant.
Sed filius Dei (qui novit sapientes in astutia sua deprehendere) eos frustratus est illicitis repudiis severè refistens: & simul tamen demonstrans nihil se nisi legi consentaneum proferre.
Nam duobus capitibus totam rem concludit: ordinem creationis

page.notes: Page number "283" is read from a worn scan and is uncertain. Running head read as NUPTIALES. after correcting the printed V to U. "malitia" is printed with a break ("malit a") and is uncertain. "infolu-" at the line end is hard to read; the word is probably insolubili. "libellu," is read as libellū with a macron for the omitted m. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. Two inline references appear in the running text: "Deut.24." and "Matth.5.", kept in place as printed. The asterisk after "repudium," is a reference mark with no matching note on the page. Left-edge and bottom stains are not transcribed. The final line appears heavier than the body but is part of the running text.
